# XHelpers Pro 1.0.9
> Notes for 1.0.9 (17). 1.0.9 is a maintenance build that carries the latest > Music & Playlists work and verifies in-app updates from 1.0.8 (16), whose > changes are listed below; 1.0.7 (15) made the Account window appear; > 1.0.6 (14) fixed a crash; 1.0.4 (12) was never published.
## What's New
- Adds AI Usage, a window that tracks the AI subscriptions you connect: Claude, Codex, Cursor, Gemini / Code Assist, GitHub Copilot, and Grok. Each account gets a card with its remaining quota and the time each window resets, with a Details view, a History view of the readings and spending already collected, a searchable list of saved connections, a monthly subscription fee you can record yourself, and optional local alerts for low quota. Readings refresh on their own while the window is open, and any account can be paused. Adding an account opens sign-in in your browser by default. A Quotas menu hides the five-hour window on 20x accounts and the Codex reserve window everywhere. Readings are collected by the bundled CodexBar helper, credited in the window and in the third-party notices. - Puts an AI button in the main menu's Tools heading showing the remaining quota of the account with the most recent activity, with account and reading details on hover, and a hover card that lists every account's quota windows and reset times. - Adds an optional YouTube connection to Music & Playlists. Connect signs in through your browser with read-only access, then imports your own playlists and Liked Videos as collections you can browse, queue, and play. Nothing is imported until you connect, the private data is removed when you disconnect or replace the account, and public YouTube imports still work signed out. An Info & Privacy sheet and a bundled connection guide describe what is read, what is stored, and how to revoke access. YouTube playback still offers no audio extraction and no offline downloads. - Plays YouTube inside XHelpers Pro's own player or in Chrome, chosen in YouTube Playback settings. The embedded player shows YouTube's complete video player in the Audio Player window, sized by YouTube's own rules and kept above full-screen apps. Its visibility rules still apply: hiding, minimizing, or fully covering the player pauses YouTube, and it picks up again once the player is visible. Closing the window, display sleep, or a locked screen needs an explicit Play. Rows YouTube will not let the app embed are kept out of the embedded player. - Lets one queue mix Apple Music, local audio, and YouTube in the order you choose, instead of playing one source's items and then the next. The Audio Player is the single place that queue plays: it shows the whole list and hands each stretch of items to the right player as playback advances. Local videos still open in Quick Video. A mixed queue is not kept between sessions, but it can be saved as one of XHelpers Pro's own mixed playlists; only a YouTube-linked playlist still has to hold a single source. Audio effects stay available while local audio is the one playing and drop out while Apple Music or YouTube has the queue. - Adds an All Songs list that gathers every song from every connected source into one flat list you can sort by column and filter, playing the whole list with Play All or just the rows you pick. - Adds Network Quality, an on-demand look at the current connection, opened from the Network section of the status menu below the Wi-Fi rows. A quick check covers the gateway, name lookup, and HTTPS reachability; a separate speed test uses macOS's own measurement. Both run only when you ask for them, results are dated and kept apart, and the menu shows a short summary. - Rebuilds the Music & Playlists Library around a source sidebar and tree: every source keeps its own section with counts and totals, an empty source offers its next step, sources are managed from the sidebar and a sheet rather than a popover, and the tree can be walked from the keyboard. Lists drop the Provider and Status columns and show format details in an Info menu, Apple Music can be sorted from its column headers, and Artist and Album stay visible in All Songs at any window width. - Reworks the Audio Player window: a smaller collapsed size, a tab that expands the transport and queue in place without moving the playback controls, a compact volume slider on hover, a draggable header, a centered title that grows to fit the artist line, and an easier resize grip. - Changes how playlists are made and saved. New Playlist now asks for a name and creates an empty playlist with an Add Songs… action instead of opening Save as Playlist with nothing to save; Save as Playlist and Add to Playlist are one sheet; Add to Playlist offers only your own custom playlists; and a playlist page's Queue menu offers Play Shuffled. - Starts every new queue with repeat off, keeps what is playing when the queue is cleared, and keeps the playback position when local audio is paused rather than restarting from the start of the segment. - Splits the old combined Utilities command into Uninstall an App and Find App Leftovers. Uninstall an App now runs as a guided session you can leave and come back to, with an All Uninstall Sessions list, per-stage review and decisions before anything is removed, and a cooperative pause, with each stage reporting what actually happened; guided sessions stay in that list once they finish. Find App Leftovers is a standalone scan for apps that are already gone. Its findings are never acted on by themselves: each item is re-checked at the moment you remove it, and removals go to the Trash only after you select them and confirm. - Removes Undo and the quarantine holding area from uninstall cleanup. Removals now either move items to the Trash as before or delete them permanently after an explicit confirmation, so nothing is kept in a private recovery area; past reports stay readable. - Rebuilds the Install Apps window: each item is a card with its own icon, grouped under section headings that flow into columns on wide windows, with search, Select All, Select None, Reset to Recommended, a plain statement of what the next run will do, progress and an outcome line while it runs, Copy Report, and a real checkbox for the PATH option. - Rebuilds Maintenance & System Tweaks as a card collection. Each tweak is a straight choice between the macOS default and the tweak, written in numbered second-person steps that name the consequence and when to use it, with the current state spelled out and confirmations shown as sheets. - Redesigns the Mac Health window with live tiles, a plain verdict, colour, and switches for the checks it keeps running, and clarifies its readings and controls. - Redesigns Clipboard History: a readable table with a type badge for Text, Link, Path, or Code, one compact line per item, relative "Copied" times, and a details panel showing the full text that can now be resized. - Shows a type specimen for every font family in Manage Fonts, installed or not: the family name set in its own face in the list, and a larger specimen with a pangram for the selected family. - Redesigns Text Tools with a tool picker, real side-by-side panes, a primary Run button, an inline status row, and on-device model settings that unlock the model tools as soon as the model's test succeeds, and moves Text Tools into the Utilities menu. - Gives every new, unnamed text document a real file of its own, saved automatically as you type and kept across closing, quitting, and restarting, so the editor no longer asks you to save a temporary document. Explicit Save is still how you choose a regular name and location, and the retained documents are reachable from the editor's file browser. - Offers XHelpers Pro in Finder's Open With for plain text and `.env` files as an alternate editor, without taking over the default handler for either. - Adds a shared Markdown viewer window with a collapsible heading outline, live search with match counts and next/previous, keyboard shortcuts, shared zoom, theme and page-width preferences, source copying, and printing. Acknowledgements and other bundled documents now open in it. - Opens Large Text Viewer and Binary Viewer as real windows instead of only a file panel, so cancelling no longer leaves nothing behind, and adds an Open… button and Command-O to the viewer toolbar. - Makes the Screen Shelf's limits configurable: the image count, the total storage, and an expiry of Never or a custom number of minutes, hours, or days, all in Shelf Settings, reached from the shelf's options menu. Existing and new shelf images default to no expiry. The shelf can also shrink to two tiles wide and one row tall in its regular view, and to a single tile when compact; previews open and close on a click without activating the app, and it has its own launch preference. - Reorganizes the status menu: Utilities is separated into six groups: text and data, audio and video, files and images, apps and fonts, Mac health, then storage and cleanup; macOS Settings Shortcuts moves to the Tools heading; Change Resolution and Keep Mac Awake open as native submenus; section headings get coloured bands and row glyphs get tints that read in light and dark menus; submenus open faster; and hover tips describe what each button does. - States permission readiness plainly: Needs attention for access that is known to be missing, Ready when the supported checks pass, Review permissions when it cannot be verified, and Checking only during the first probe. Unsupported macOS features no longer count as missing, hover text names the exact items, and the permissions dialog now summarizes by tier and fits on short screens. - Lets the System Settings shortcut cards be rearranged by dragging, and gives Global Shortcuts compact category tabs with a window that fits its tallest tab and remembers its size. - Connects the account sign-in forms to the macOS Passwords app, remembers the email addresses you have signed in with, starts Google and Apple sign-in in your browser at the provider's own page and returns you to a styled page when it finishes, and cancels a pending provider sign-in if you close the Account window. - Separates Account and License in the main menu: the row's left side opens Account and a separate right-aligned button with a seal and a License status opens license management. The Account window now shows this Mac's local activation only; linking a license to a Xin account has been removed. Saved-key validation, revalidation, and offline grace are unchanged. - Gives XHelpers Pro a new app icon. - Opens windows and dialogs at a size that shows their content, and stops the scrollbar flash and the transient scrollbars that appeared while a window was still laying itself out, including Finder-opened editor windows, AI Settings as its disclosures expand, Mac Health, Network Quality, Image Tools, and the Markdown viewer. - Fixes a batch of correctness problems found in a review pass: Extract Audio now reports a cancelled export honestly instead of hanging in a stopping state; Quick Video cannot restart a load that is already preparing; PDF operations escape a stalled stop and report both rollback causes; Image Tools keeps redaction edges opaque and exports more safely; archive extraction handles more common TAR layouts, skips AppleDouble entries, and reveals finished extractions; saving text ignores metadata-only changes and names a refused symlink; and a stopped step of an app install is recorded as cancelled rather than failed. - Fixes crashes and stalls when navigating playlists, restores playback after an audio stall or an end-of-file seek, and restores the menu icons that went missing on macOS 27. - Fixes smaller annoyances: resizing an image in Image Tools now keeps its aspect ratio, Finder menus no longer overlap during a local app install, mouse profiles are reapplied when HID services reconnect, changing the app language no longer stalls behind a deferred document save, and the app can quit while a sheet is attached. - Redesigns the Account window: a centered layout with the Xin mark, one clear next action, left-aligned sign-in buttons, and a status line that only shows what applies. Sign-in, enrollment, license linking, and deletion keep the same behavior. - Fixes the Account window not appearing: its section boxes were constrained to the layout before joining it, which AppKit rejected while the window was being built. The window now also brings XHelpers Pro to the front. - Fixes a crash when choosing Account… or other menu actions on macOS 14 and later, and the same crash in Clipboard History capture: a main-thread isolation check inside a timer callback failed inside the Swift runtime. - Adds an optional Xin account. Sign in with an email address and password, an emailed sign-in code, Google, or Sign in with Apple, then enroll the account in XHelpers, and manage the linked sign-in methods from the Account window. Every local tool and local Pro activation keeps working signed out and offline; the account is never required. The Account window can delete XHelpers data, the whole Xin account, or just the sign-in identity, each with a fresh sign-in and each resumable if interrupted. Session and recovery state stay in this Mac's Keychain, and XHelpers Pro never stores a Google or Apple password. The privacy policy and license agreement describe exactly what the account service keeps. - Live Subtitles can now show captions in the spoken language without translating. Switch between Translate and Captions only at the top of the Configure window's Languages section, or flip the Captions Only row in the status menu, which restarts a listening session in the new mode. The status-menu row, shortcut, and Configure window are now titled Live Subtitles. - Adds Quick Audio, a fast local player for user-supplied MP3, M4A (AAC or ALAC), AAC/ADTS, WAVE/BWF, AIFF, AIFF-C, FLAC, and CAF files, with an ephemeral queue that is discarded when the player closes. - Makes the supported formats available in Open With without taking over defaults; Audio Player Settings provides a separate opt-in action and can restore the previous default handlers while XHelpers Pro still owns them. - Adds Music & Playlists for browsing and playing songs made available through Apple Music and for creating private playlists owned by XHelpers Pro. Apple Music access is requested only after you choose Connect, never at launch, and the feature does not create or change playlists in Music.app. Provider-safe live queues can be extended, replaced, or explicitly saved as a new XHelpers Pro playlist. - Adds Local Audio playlists and a private on-Mac index for only the files and folders you select, with source reauthorization, missing-file repair, and separate delete/reset controls that never change the original audio files. - Adds Local Video to Music & Playlists: a private on-Mac index of only the video files and folders you select, with its own sources, missing-video repair, source reauthorization, and a separate delete control. It obeys the same source-authorization and deletion rules as Local Audio and never changes the original video files. Choosing a video plays it in Quick Video, and a Quick Video queue can be saved as a Local Video playlist. - Stores Music & Playlists data in XHelpers Pro's private, size-bounded local SQLite database with up to three daily recovery snapshots. Successful provider-data deletion or full reset clears all Music & Playlists recovery snapshots and database recovery/journal files. The app declares file-timestamp access for user-selected files and directories under Apple's required privacy-manifest reason 3B52.1. - Adds Extract Audio for pulling the soundtrack out of videos into new M4A (AAC or Apple Lossless), MP3, or WAV files, or copying AAC, Apple Lossless, and PCM tracks without re-encoding. Videos are never modified and outputs never overwrite existing files. MP3 output uses the bundled LAME encoder library, disclosed in the third-party notices. - Adds Quick Video, a small floating player for the formats QuickTime plays (MP4, MOV, M4V, 3GP), with speed, loop, always-on-top, frame stepping, and Picture in Picture. Any frame can be opened in Image Tools, added to the Screen Shelf, or copied, and the file can be sent straight to Extract Audio. Live Subtitles can run on the video being played, taken from the player's own audio and pinned to the player window. Video types are offered in Open With without taking over defaults; unsupported files are handed to your default video app. - Gives Quick Video a playback queue in the same list Quick Audio uses. Dropping files, Open Video…, and Open With add to the queue of the player you are already using instead of opening one window per file; rows can be reordered, played next, or removed, loop is now off, one, or all, and New Player Window starts a second, independent queue. The queue exists only while that window is open and is never saved. - Gives Quick Video the Audio Player's audio effects. Audio Effects… in the player's options menu opens the same panel, over the same settings kept per output device, so adjusting the chain in either place applies to both. A video's audio is processed as it plays, and Live Subtitles hear what you hear. - Gives both players the same queue controls: Shuffle, Repeat off, one, or all, and Play Next, which moves the rows you picked directly behind the one that is playing. Shuffle deals a fresh order each time you turn it on and skips a row it cannot play, exactly as the queue does. - Brings the Audio Player's features out of the ⋯ menu. Shuffle, Repeat, Audio Effects, Live Subtitles, and Add to Queue are now buttons under the transport, each showing its own state: shuffle and repeat light up while they are on, repeat says whether it is the whole queue or one song, Audio Effects lights up while the output you are listening on has effects applied, and Live Subtitles lights up while it is running for the player. The row stays in place with an empty queue, so adding files, shuffle, repeat, and the effects chain are still one click away, and the window is no taller than before. The ⋯ menu keeps the rarer things: Play Audio…, Audio Player Settings…, Reveal Current File in Finder, and Clear Queue. - Lets a live queue hold local audio and local video together. Songs play in Quick Audio and videos in Quick Video, so a mixed list keeps the music where it belongs and opens the picture where you can see it. Apple Music and YouTube still keep a queue of their own, and Music & Playlists now says so on Add to Queue before you press it rather than in a sheet afterwards. A saved playlist can mix sources; only a YouTube-linked playlist is restricted to one. - Offers the same media actions wherever an item appears. Extract Audio, Open Frame in Image Tools, Add Frame to Screen Shelf, Copy Frame, and Live Subtitles are decided in one place and shown by both player toolbars, the queue rows, and the Music & Playlists rows, each offering only what that item can really do: no Extract Audio for a song, no frame actions for a row that is not on screen, and Live Subtitles only for what is playing. - Runs Live Subtitles for a video on the player's own audio inside XHelpers Pro instead of tapping this app's audio process, so a video from your own library can be subtitled with nothing else listened to. Browser audio still uses the process capture it always did, and the subtitles overlay is still pinned to the player window. Subtitle text, captured frames, and queues are still never saved. - Adds Image Tools for straightforward resize, crop, rotate, flip, markup, redaction, format conversion, metadata choices, and bounded batch output. - Adds Capture to Clipboard and Capture & Mark Up to the existing Screen Tools selector, keeping captures in memory until an explicit destination is chosen. - Expands local health guidance into Why Is My Mac Slow?, combining plain- language CPU, memory, startup-volume, and thermal evidence with safe actions. - Adds PDF Quick Actions for combining PDFs, organizing pages, extracting or splitting pages, and creating PDFs from images, with a PDF-only Finder action. - Adds Startup & Background Inspector for reviewing login items and background agents with direct System Settings guidance. - Retains the existing opt-in memory monitoring engine as part of Mac Health's broader local slowdown evidence. - Adds Text Tools and a first-class Text Editor for plain text and Markdown, including split/preview layouts, syntax highlighting, and text-size controls. - Adds private, on-device Live Translated Subtitles for selected browser audio, with speaker-aware cues and fullscreen tracking on macOS 26.4 or later. - Expands file and Markdown viewing with multiple windows, large-text, binary, hexadecimal, and persistent text-size support. - Reorganizes the menu bar into a compact two-column layout with keyboard access to its submenus and clearer utility and screen-tool groups. - Improves Window Recall activation/focus verification and keeps Snap & Arrange state current, keyboard-accessible, and stable after submenu refreshes. - Improves subtitle placement across fullscreen Spaces and stabilizes speaker colors, source lines, and translated cues.
## Initial 1.0.0 Highlights
- Introduces XHelpers Pro as the direct-download flagship Mac utility app. - Includes display tools for mirrored MacBook display blackout, brightness, contrast, dim-until-key-press, and keyboard backlight control. - Adds optional Auto Wi-Fi Switch for saved Wi-Fi networks, with signal threshold controls and local-only Wi-Fi scanning. - Adds Finder context menu actions for creating files and folders, pasting copied items, copying paths, and opening Finder selections in configured apps such as TextEdit, Terminal, Codex, Claude, or VSCode. - Adds local Safe archive actions for encrypting selected files or folders into a `.safe` file, adding items to an existing Safe, and decrypting Safes back to local folders. - Lets users configure the default terminal, default editor, enabled Finder menu items, saved folder grants, Full Disk Access guidance, and copy-path escaping. - Ships with a new XHelpers Pro icon and Sparkle update support.
## Install
1. Open the DMG. 2. Drag `XHelpers Pro.app` onto `Applications`. 3. Open XHelpers Pro from Applications.
The app appears in the macOS menu bar.
## Compatibility
Compatibility note: this direct-download app uses macOS capabilities that may not be suitable for a Mac App Store build and may change in future macOS updates.
Requires macOS 14.0 or later.
